The ranking is unstable and several models share correlated errors, so a robust weighted scheme that down‑weights high‑error models while still using all models may beat DBA.
The series has strong seasonality and unstable ranking (tau -0.045), so a robust median combination may outperform weighted/DBA.
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality; a trimmed mean may reduce influence of outlier models.
trend is very strong and ranking unstable, so a simple mean may reduce variance and serve as a robust baseline for comparison.
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality, so a per‑horizon weighted mean may capture horizon‑specific best performers.
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality; a simple inverse‑error weighted mean may outperform the current best top‑k mean per horizon.
Ranking is unstable and several correlated groups exist; a per‑horizon best‑model weighting may capture changing strengths across the 8‑step horizon.
ranking is unstable and seasonality strong, so a per‑horizon weighted mean may still help; try a different top‑k per‑horizon weight handle (w6) which was not scored yet.
seasonality is extremely strong and ranking unstable; a softmax weighted mean on the top‑trend/seasonal models (pool4) may capture the dominant signal without over‑fitting.
Test a simple robust mean over the stable pool of 7 top models (trend, seasonality, ranking unstable) to see if averaging improves over weighted.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted weighted by w4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9667. Series context: trend strength 0.9991 and seasonal strength 0.9999; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.045); 4 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.604.
